messages:
alex: Heads up — after we shipped the shaded Android client I noticed hundreds of sockets stuck in TIME_WAIT on staging. Looks like OkHttp connections aren't being released. Anyone run into this when shading jackson or gson?

sana: Yep, ran into a similar smell. In our case a parse error aborted a streaming read and the ResponseBody never got closed, leaving connections open.

mike: This is a classic: if you use Jackson's MappingIterator or readValues on a Reader/Stream you must close the ResponseBody (or the iterator) on all code paths. GC-based cleanup is too slow to keep connection counts sane.

alex: We're doing something like:
```
MappingIterator<Event> it = mapper.readerFor(Event.class).readValues(resp.body().charStream());
while (it.hasNext()) {
  handle(it.next());
}
```
And sometimes we break out early or a parse error happens.

sana: That exact pattern leaks. Wrap resp.body() in try-with-resources or ensure you call resp.body().close() in finally. Also prefer byteStream() when using Jackson streaming (binary-safe). Example fix:
```
try (ResponseBody rb = resp.body()) {
  MappingIterator<Event> it = mapper.readerFor(Event.class).readValues(rb.byteStream());
  while (it.hasNext()) process(it.next());
}
```

liz: Another thing to check: our shadowJar relocation moved com.fasterxml.jackson.* to a shaded package and some libs that use ServiceLoader still tried to load the original names, causing reflective failures that aborted parsing before close. If you relocated jackson, that could be the root.

alex: We do relocate jackson in shadowJar:
```
shadowJar {
  relocate 'com.fasterxml.jackson', 'shade.com.fasterxml.jackson'
  mergeServiceFiles()
}
```

mike: Relocating jackson is fragile. It can break ServiceLoader, module-info, and any runtime reflection expectations. Better to exclude jackson from the jar or avoid relocating it.

sana: If shading is unavoidable, make sure to relocate ServiceLoader metadata and any known entrypoints. But honestly excluding jackson is usually the simpler, less error-prone path.

alex: Short-term mitigations we can roll right away?

liz: 1) Add try-with-resources on all streaming code paths so bodies get closed. 2) Rebuild shadowJar excluding com.fasterxml.jackson packages (or stop relocating them). 3) Add logging/metrics for parse exceptions so we catch these earlier.

mike: Also as a temporary band-aid you can tune OkHttp's ConnectionPool to evict faster so sockets don't pile up during the rollout:
```
new OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .connectionPool(new ConnectionPool(5, 2, TimeUnit.MINUTES))
  .dispatcher(new Dispatcher(Executors.newCachedThreadPool()))
  .build();
```
But that's a workaround — fix the unclosed bodies.

alex: I'll open a PR that (A) wraps streaming responses with try-with-resources, (B) removes jackson relocation from our shadowJar, and (C) emits a metric on JSON parse failures.

ci-bot: CI triggered for PR #402 — build queued.

sana: Ping me once the PR is up, I can run a staging load to confirm sockets drain.

alex: Awesome, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
